title: [YouPass Collect] - International tourist arrivals comparison 2009-2010
prompt: The table compares the international tourist arrivals in millions in 9 countries in 2009 and 2010 and the changes (in percentages). Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the changes in visits from overseas to 9 countries, in both absolute and relative terms, in two consecutive years, namely 2009 and 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, with the exception of France and Hong Kong, all the countries welcomed more tourists in 2010. In addition, France was the most popular destination, while the most significant growth was seen in Germany.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the most visited nations, in 2009, while 66 million people traveled to the US, Spain and the UK each attracted 55 million tourists, which was 11 million higher than Italy. An increase from 1 to 2 million was subsequently witnessed in these countries, equivalent to 1.5% to 3.6% growth. Meanwhile, France's number topped the list at 76 million in 2009, and remained unchanged in the following year.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: With regard to the remaining countries, the number of visitors to Turkey was 33 million, 11 million higher than that of China, which in turn outnumbered the next country, Germany, by the same margin. There was a rise of 12 million in the figures for all the 3 nations, with their relative growth being 33%, 55% and 109%, respectively. Hong Kong was the least appealing tourist destination, with its numbers declining from 10 to 9 million in 2010, representing a drop of 11%.
